sections.title: Sections
sections.lede: The catalogue is a frozen public contract – a number is never reused, and a retired section becomes a no-op that says so.
sections.reportOnlyTitle: Report only - there is nothing to select
sections.detailReportOnly: This section writes a report and deletes nothing.
sections.detailNothing: Nothing declared on this machine right now.
sections.emptyBody: All {{count}} are still there. The filter is narrow.
sections.policySummary: What the four run policies mean
sections.policyBody: <1>Safe</1> runs on its own. <3>Opt-in</3> only runs if you name it. <5>Deep</5> needs an extra confirmation on top. <7>Interactive</7> needs you to pick the items, one by one.
sections.selBlocked: Sections {{ids}} need you to choose items first. Nothing was run.
picker.section.17.title: Stale build artefacts
picker.section.17.lede: node_modules, target, .gradle and friends, in projects nothing has touched for months. Rebuilt by the project’s own install or build command.
picker.section.18.title: Partial downloads
picker.section.18.lede: Half-finished downloads left behind by browsers and download managers. Only Downloads – never Desktop, never Documents.
picker.section.19.title: Large personal files
picker.section.19.lede: Anything over the size threshold that has not been opened in a long time. These go to the Recycle Bin.
picker.section.23.title: Orphaned application data
picker.section.23.lede: AppData folders belonging to programs that are no longer installed. Fails closed: if the registry cannot be read, nothing is offered.
picker.notAskedBody: A dry-run costs nothing and deletes nothing.
picker.devOff: Developer mode is off, so the engine skips this one. Turn it on in Settings first.
picker.searchEmptyBody: Clear the filter and the candidates come back.
picker.note: <1>Nothing here is pre-selected, on purpose.</1> These four sections refuse to act on <3>--yes</3> alone – the prompt still appears, the default is none, and the final question is never auto-answered. A scripted selection (<5>--select</5> or <7>--select-file</7>) counts as a person choosing, and only then does the run go ahead unattended.
picker.fileSummary: Drive this from a file instead
picker.fileBody: A plain UTF-8 file with one full path per line is matched, case-insensitively, against the candidates this section offers. A line that matches nothing is warned about individually rather than failing the run.
picker.fileTipPurpose: <1>Purpose: </1>One full path per line; each is matched against the candidates a section offers.
picker.fileIdle: Drop a selection file here, or choose one
picker.fileHint: .txt or .list · up to 256 KB · one full path per line
picker.fileTooBig: That file is {{size}} - the limit is 256 KB
picker.fileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
picker.nothingHereBody: This section found no candidates on this machine. That is the good outcome, not an error.
picker.consequence: The Recycle Bin can be emptied later. Permanent has no undo.
picker.consequence17: Section 17's rows are deleted outright whichever you choose; this choice covers 18, 19 and 23.
picker.confirmBody: They do not go to the Recycle Bin. Permanent has no undo.
elevation.title_one: {{count}} section needs Windows to ask your permission.
elevation.title_other: {{count}} sections need Windows to ask your permission.
elevation.lede: windowsweep <1>never elevates itself</1>. When you ask for one of these, it opens a second, elevated window that does that work and writes its own report. This window keeps running, unelevated, and shows you the log as it arrives.
elevation.whatHappens: What happens when you press it
elevation.step.asks.title: Windows asks you.
elevation.step.asks.body: The standard User Account Control prompt, from Windows, not from windowsweep. If you say no, nothing happens and nothing is written.
elevation.step.second.title: A second window opens.
elevation.step.second.body: It runs only the sections you chose, with <1>--reports-dir</1> and <3>--logs-dir</3> pointed at this run’s folder.
elevation.step.tails.title: This window tails the log.
elevation.step.tails.body: You watch it from here. The elevated window closes itself when it is done, and its exit code comes back to this one.
elevation.step.reports.title: Both reports land side by side.
elevation.hiberfilLegend: What to do with the hibernation file
elevation.devOff: Developer mode is off, so the engine skips this one. Turn it on in Settings first.
elevation.deepGateTitle: Two of these cannot be undone, and one changes how Windows starts.
elevation.deepGateBody: windowsweep will not run them unattended until you say you know that – it passes <3>--i-understand-deep</3>, and nothing else in this window does.
elevation.deepWhat.15: <1>Hibernation file.</1> Turning it off removes <3>hiberfil.sys</3> and with it Hibernate, Fast Startup and hibernate-on-critical-battery. Sleep still works. Reduced keeps Fast Startup at a smaller file.
elevation.deepWhat.16: <1>Event logs.</1> Clearing them is permanent and removes the history a technician would use to diagnose a problem.
elevation.deepWhat.20: <1>WSL disk images.</1> Compaction stops Docker Desktop and every WSL distro first. Start Docker again afterwards.
elevation.deepConfirm: I understand what these do. Run the ones I chose.
elevation.deepConfirmAria: I understand what these sections do
elevation.blockedNone: Choose at least one section first.
elevation.blockedDeep: Confirm you understand the deep sections above.
elevation.childReport: The elevated window reclaimed {{amount}} across $t(elevation.countSteps, {"count": {{ran}} }), and skipped {{skipped}}.
elevation.measureNote: A scan can measure these sections without administrator rights. It cannot clear them.
elevation.measured: Measured {{amount}} across the sections you chose. Nothing was deleted, and no permission was needed to look.
elevation.smartScreenSummary: Windows may warn you the first time you install this
elevation.smartScreenWhy: The installer is not signed with a paid code-signing certificate, so Microsoft SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC” on first run. That is a statement about the certificate, not about the file.
elevation.smartScreenHow: Choose More info and then Run anyway. You can verify what you downloaded first: every release publishes a SHA-256 checksum for each installer, and a minisign signature the app’s own updater checks. Neither is a code-signing certificate – they prove the file is the one that was built, not who built it. The source is public.
elevation.smartScreenWhyHere: This note is here rather than hidden because meeting that dialog unexplained is worse than reading about it in advance.
